objects.original: The actual joint coefficient Gaussian on the direct sum of ordered Euclidean tensor blocks, and the literal radial level fields H_i built from Eq. (15) and Eq. (16).
objects.reconstructed: One standard Gaussian on the flat sigma-indexed Euclidean space; coordinate restriction gives each (i,p) tensor, and H evaluates the deterministic cutoff times the sum of angular tensor contractions, with the prescribed zero branch.
objects.evidence: Eq. (15) is an entrywise inner product. For each copy l in Fin p and each slot (j,k) with k < K^j, the tensor entry uses u_j at its assigned coordinate. Its product over slots and sum against the original coefficients is exactly angularDegreeComponent. The extract/wrap operations preserve entries: no fresh draw, permutation of a level's tail, or symmetric quotient.

domains.original: All h+1 n-dimensional spatial blocks, level indices 0 through h, and even degrees from 4 through P inclusive. Each level uses the tail from i through h.
domains.reconstructed: A point in Fin (h+1) -> EuclideanSpace R (Fin n); levels Fin (h+1), the even >=4 subtype of Fin (P+1), and coordinates indexed by all maps from p copies of the relative tail slots into Fin n.
domains.evidence: The relative j in Fin (h-i+1) corresponds bijectively to absolute i+j, so K^j is precisely K^(absolute index - i). The finite upper bound is inclusive since Fin (P+1) is strict at P+1. There are p S_i slots and n^(p S_i) ordered entries per block, including when h=i.

quantifiers.original: Within the hard-family regime (large n, prescribed h), Section 6.1 fixes one deterministic full x and evaluates all level fields together under the original coefficient law.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For all positive n and natural h and every deterministic full x, one pushforward under the single coefficient law contains every level i at that same x.
quantifiers.evidence: The exposed finite-identity generalization drops the unrelated large-n/depth relation; no step from Eq. (14)-(16), the diagonal of Lemma 4.4, or finite independent grouping needs it. Quantifying x outside HasLaw preserves the fixed-x scope and does not assert simultaneous independence over locations.

assumptions.original: Standard Gaussian tensor blocks are jointly independent under mu_n by construction. Zero participating blocks are covered by zero extension, not excluded.
assumptions.reconstructed: The input measure is exactly stdGaussian of the full Euclidean coefficient space. No independence, positive cutoff, nonzero x, normalization regularity, or measurability hypothesis is added.
assumptions.evidence: jointCoefficientBlocks_hasLaw establishes the product for the actual full input measure. The nonzero-tail branch derives the normalization condition internally in radialLevel_hasLaw; the zero branch uses chi(0)=0. Measurability of each field as a function of coefficients is proved by a constant/finite-linear branch split.

conclusion.original: At fixed x, Lemma 4.4 gives independent centered degree variables with variances n C_i(x)^2 a_{i,p}^2. The Section 6.1 calculation sums the degree variables by level before weighting.
conclusion.reconstructed: The exact joint pushforward is the finite product of centered Gaussian laws of variances n c_i^2 sum_p a_{i,p}^2, including point masses at zero.
conclusion.evidence: Independent degree sums over disjoint coefficient groups are mutually independent and have variance sum of the degree variances. The Lean proof reindexes the actual product, curries it by level, pushes forward each measurable factor and identifies its law by radialLevel_hasLaw at that same tail. All variance factors are nonnegative, so toNNReal preserves the actual real number. gaussianReal_zero_var is dirac 0 for center 0; cutoff-zero factors need no density or nondegeneracy.

scopes.original: The unconditioned fixed-x scalar law is an intermediate result, not the whole covariance lemma or the later energy-test and conditional calculations.
scopes.reconstructed: One vector of level field values at one fixed x under one unconditioned coefficient draw. No weights or conditioning enter HasLaw.
scopes.evidence: Eq. (13) distinguishes the radial field from the gated truncated load. The theorem contains no gate, truncation, beta weight, MGF, second location, derivative, prefix sigma-field or conditioning event. Section 6.1 immediately before Eq. (51) is the use site, not a claim to prove the equation or Section 6.2.

constant_dependencies.original: K=2^(74(h+1)), P=2^(64(h+1)), S_i=sum_(j=0)^(h-i) K^j and a_{i,p}=1/(p^4 S_i^2 sqrt((h-i+1) log(2 P S_i))). Footnote 2 uses the unscaled rho quotients at 0.65, 0.70, 0.95, 1; v_i is the angular sum of squares.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same powers, relative slots, natural log, amplitude and radial thresholds occur literally. The reconstruction labels the final variance v_i rather than the paper's unscaled v_i; its formula includes exactly n c_i^2.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The rational thresholds 13/20, 7/10, 19/20, 1 and expNegInvGlue equal the source cutoffs. The production outer S elaborates as a real sum whereas the reused angular/marginal S is a natural sum cast to the reals. hSlots rewrites exactly by Nat.cast_sum, Nat.cast_pow and Nat.cast_ofNat, with identical exponents and indices. There is no amplitude or variance change.

deltas.description: The entrywise tensor model is represented by finite assignment indices and regrouped as a dependent product without changing entries.
The finite identity is stated for all positive n and natural h, without applying that generalization to admissibility or lower bounds.
The product pushforward and its variance-zero Dirac factors make the fixed-point intermediate grouping explicit.
The blind reconstruction uses v_i for the full variance. Its formula equals n C_i(x)^2 times the source v_i; the natural-slot cast and real slot sum are equal.
